chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Jawhari, from Aban ibn Uthman, from Ismail al-Ju'fi and Ma'mar ibn Yahya, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"The Qunut is before the Ruku', and if you wish, it is after it."

His saying 'and if you wish, it is after it' is interpreted as referring to the state of making up (Qada) or precaution (Taqiyyah), according to the view of some of the Sunnis regarding the morning prayer.
ai.seo_question: When can the Qunut be recited in relation to Ruku' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) confirms the permissibility of performing Qunut either before or after Ruku', reflecting the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding supplication timing. The commentary contextualizes the 'after Ruku'' option as applicable to Qada (make-up) prayers or Taqiyyah, aligning with certain Sunni views on the Fajr prayer, while highlighting the scholarly nuance in distinguishing between obligatory and recommended timings. This hadith is foundational in the chapter of prayer mechanics within Tahdhib al-Ahkam, illustrating the practical application of divine guidance in ritual worship.
